newsitem.title: TURKEY: Israel's foreign minister to visit Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Israel's foreign minister to visit Turkey.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will make a two-day visit to Turkey next month, the first high-level visit since both countries formed new governments last summer, an Israeli embassy official said on Tuesday.
"There will be a visit of Mr. Levy on the 8th and 9th of April," the official told Reuters.
Relations between overwhelmingly Moslem but officially secular Turkey and the Jewish state have been boosted by two military accords sealed last year.

The accords, condemned by Iran, many in the Arab world and some Islamists in Turkey, allow Israeli jets on training flights to use Turkish airspace and arranged for Israel to upgrade the Turkish air force's F-4 jets.
Since becoming prime minister last June in a coalition with conservative secularists, Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his criticism of closer relations with Israel.
Turkey's chief of staff, Ismail Hakki Karadayi, visited Israel in February and then described the links between the two countries as the relations between "the only democracies in the region."
